title: The remote viewing photo protocol and its 35% hit rate, replicated at Edinburgh and the Rhine institute
place_text: SRI; University of Edinburgh; Rhine Research Institute, Duke, North Carolina

tellings.quote: the study of these attempts found that there was an overall hit rate of 35% a number that was found to be repeatable over and over again

plain: Tests of remote viewing, the claimed ability to describe a distant place or hidden photo with the mind, are said to have reached an overall hit rate of 35 percent, a figure found "repeatable over and over again" at the Stanford Research Institute, the University of Edinburgh and the Rhine Research Institute in North Carolina. Michels tells it himself, citing a review of the studies tied to the statistician Jessica Utts, while talking with a writer named Eric Wargo. If the rate holds, people would be doing better than chance at seeing what they cannot see.
